### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/datasource.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/datasource.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/virtual-objects.mdx`  _(via rowCap (symbol, a method of interface ExternalDriverFloorHost))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/datasource.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/datasource.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9edd6e783b48ad5e326060e4c4c35040f159deac` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `277332d4729c989998874d133564399db3a37b45` — the merge of head `0ca2cf4934d53b7b890627644d2d574be236c76e` into base `9edd6e783b48ad5e326060e4c4c35040f159deac`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 277332d4729c989998874d133564399db3a37b45 && git checkout 277332d4729c989998874d133564399db3a37b45
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9edd6e783b48ad5e326060e4c4c35040f159deac 0ca2cf4934d53b7b890627644d2d574be236c76e && git checkout -B drift-repro 9edd6e783b48ad5e326060e4c4c35040f159deac && git merge --no-ff 0ca2cf4934d53b7b890627644d2d574be236c76e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9edd6e783b48ad5e326060e4c4c35040f159deac
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9edd6e783b48ad5e326060e4c4c35040f159deac` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3f1cd437e05db18dd78f39ce1bd15084a38baf81`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`DatasourceDef`, `registerDatasourceDef`, `applyExternalDriverFloor`, `listDatasourceDefs`), packages/objectql/src/external-driver-floor.ts (`ExternalDriverFloorHost`, `readCapped`), packages/objectql/src/external-driver-errors.ts (`EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP`, `resolveExternalRowCap`, `ExternalRowCapExceededError`), packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts (the authored key, on `main` since #29854), packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-connection-service.ts (the producer, `:865` and `:1101`), packages/objectql/src/plugin-driver-conformance.ts (`ROW_LIMIT`), packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.test.ts (the mutual-extends pin on the def)

Inputs read: card #29762 (body; every comment through the dev's final report 6599918138, including ruling 6597043019, the claim amendment 6597054809, the measurement 6595439927 and the #29854 record 6598079463), PR #29876 (body, 11-file list, net diff against `main` at the head), and the head's check-runs (two reads). The remainder of the diff (changeset, the two guides, liveness row and state count, the objectql and spec tests) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; it was read, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/contracts`**: `EngineDatasourceDef.external` gains `rowCap?: number`. Optional member on an interface two members (`registerDatasourceDef?`, `listDatasourceDefs?`) take and answer; a widening only. `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` list the interface by name, not by member, so no shard moves. **Right.**
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/objectql`**: `DatasourceDef.external.rowCap?: number` (the structurally-identical twin the contract's docblock names); `ExternalDriverFloorHost.rowCap?(): unknown` (optional host callback); `EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP` keeps its export and its value, now bound to `EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP_DEFAULT`; `resolveExternalRowCap` is module-internal, not re-exported from `index.ts`; `ExternalRowCapExceededError`'s message grows a clause below the ceiling and `details.cap` now carries the datasource's cap. All widenings. **Right.**
- **Accept-set, engine**: a floored datasource reads at most `resolveExternalRowCap(def.external?.rowCap)` rows per request: a whole number in [1, 10000] is used as written, above 10,000 is held at the ceiling, anything else (absent, 0, negative, fractional, NaN, a string, null) is the default 1,000. Defs that came through `DatasourceSchema` (the admin write door parses at `datasource-admin-service.ts:1324`; code-defined datasources parse through the stack) never reach the clamp or the fallback; both exist for a host calling the public `registerDatasourceDef` contract directly. The platform maximum is never exceeded from any door. **Right.**
- **Accept-set, authored metadata**: unchanged by this diff. `ExternalDatasourceSettingsSchema.rowCap` and its refusals landed in #29854; this PR moves no `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` shard. What changes is that the key is now read. **Right as a tree; see ② on how it is declared.**
- **Liveness**: `external.rowCap` flips `planned` to `live` with evidence on `createExternalDriverFloor` (`const cap = resolveExternalRowCap(host.rowCap?.())`) and `applyExternalDriverFloor` (the `rowCap` callback reading `this.datasourceDefs.get(name)?.external?.rowCap` at call time), and a `producer` on `attemptConnect`. Verified against the tree: both cited lines exist at the head; the producer passes `record.external` whole (`:869`, `:1105` — the `as { allowWrites?: boolean }` cast narrows the type only, the object reaches the engine with every key), so an authored `rowCap` arrives on connect and reconnect. The parent note is rewritten to "7 of 7 live" with the #4583 history of the two removed keys. `Spec property liveness`: success. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29762-external-row-cap-floor.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': minor`, `'@objectstack/spec': minor`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`, both line-initial in the changeset and the PR body, identical wording. `Check Changeset`: completed, success (the level axis reads `clean`: a kind beside `minor`).
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is true of the tree (the interface and host widenings in ①).
- The kind is where I disagree with the declaration, on the rule's own definition (AGENTS.md rule 3: "the change to what a metadata author can write — a new key … is `added`"). This diff adds no authorable key, value or type; #29854 did, and declared `added` for it. What this diff changes is what the engine does with a key an author can already write — the strict reading is `none` (level `patch` on both packages), and the most that can be argued is `semantic` (the authored key goes from inert to enforced). `added` restates PR 1's kind on PR 2 and earns a second `minor` for the same key. Not a FAIL: both lines are declared and mutually consistent, the gate is green, and over-grading is the semver-safe direction; the checker enforces only that `none` never sits beside `minor`. **Should-fix 1.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The six items carried from the #29854 record (6598079463)** — each checked in the tree, not the PR body:
  1. `maxRowCount` in the alias message test — landed (`datasource.test.ts:999`, the loop now runs `maxRows`, `rowLimit`, `maxRowCount`).
  2. `EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP` rebound to `EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP_DEFAULT`, docblock rewritten — landed (`external-driver-errors.ts:33-41`; the "not an authorable key" sentence is gone, ruling 2 on #27261 is kept as history beside #29762).
  3. The cap passed into `ExternalRowCapExceededError` — landed (`external-driver-floor.ts:223`, third argument; `details.cap` pinned by test).
  4. The cap read per `readCapped` call from the current `datasourceDefs` entry — landed (`external-driver-floor.ts:202` reads `host.rowCap?.()` on every call; `engine.ts:9950-9952` closes over `name` and reads the map at call time, which is exactly what survives the early `if (floored) return` at `:9940`). The test "a redefinition applies to the next read without re-wrapping the driver" pins both the same held instance and the new limit.
  5. `DatasourceDef.external.rowCap` — landed (`engine.ts:4736-4741`), with the contract twin in the `hits` file. `listDatasourceDefs` spreads `external`, so the read-back carries it and the mutual-extends pin in `data-engine.test.ts:626-641` still resolves (`Registered` and `Listed` both now carry the member).
  6. Liveness row `live` citing the reader; parent note fixed — landed (see ①).
- **Dev report `open_questions`**: the 2,000-row whole-set view ceiling (`NON_GRID_ROW_CEILING`, objectui#7210 ruling a′), options A leave / B ui-lane card on a customer pull. Ruling 6597043019 explicitly did not rule on it, and the guide's new "Views that read the whole set" section states both ceilings and what a planner gets in each band, so the customer is told the truth about a 5,000-row gantt (first 2,000 rows with the note). **Escalated to the seat as the dev recommends: B only on a customer pull; nothing in this PR forecloses it.**
- **Out-of-scope finding, conformance kit**: `ROW_LIMIT = EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP + 1` (`plugin-driver-conformance.ts:507`) is unchanged, and the kit's own floors (`writeCase`, `flooredRead`) pass no `rowCap` host, so every kit read is at the default. The measurement asked for "one case that sends another limit and checks the driver honours it"; the dev answers that no small-fixture case can detect a driver that hard-codes 1001, and the guide now carries the rule ("Never hard-code `1001`"). I judged the answer: a driver that stops paging the remote at 1,001 rows is indistinguishable from a correct one on any fixture under 1,002 rows, so the dev is right that the existing fixtures cannot see it; a case that could would need a generated fixture above 1,001 rows and a raised-cap floor host. That is a kit change with its own cost, not this card's. **Answered; should-fix 3 names the follow-up.**
- **Out-of-scope finding, the service cast** `record.external as { allowWrites?: boolean }` at the two `registerDatasourceDef` calls: type-only narrowing, the whole block flows at runtime (verified above). Harmless today; a future reader could believe the engine receives only `allowWrites`. Noted, not filed, as the dev says. **Answered.**
- `Skills-docs: updated here` names `virtual-objects.mdx` and `odata-datasources.mdx`. Read for the claims they make about the code: `limit` cap + 1 (`:437`), the two reads per list page (`:623`, matches `count` re-reading through `readCapped`), the schema refusals (match #29854), the 2,001-row ask and 2,000-row ceiling (match the measurement), the "35 ms and 2 MiB at 10,000" figures (match the measurement table). No claim contradicts the tree. Lane seat's remainder.

### ④ Design judgment

File: `packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts`. Judged against the contract's own rule in its docblock ("the keys are a deliberate SUBSET of the spec's authored datasource surface — the engine retains only what it has a use for. ⛔ Not a mirror of the authored block and not a place to grow one … [#12805] mirrors engine reality, it does not invent surface"), against the engine that implements the member, and against the scenario the card accepts it for (a plugin-driver datasource that sets `rowCap: 5000` reads 5,000 rows per request from the moment it is registered or re-registered).

- **The member is engine reality, not invented surface.** The same diff makes the engine read it (`applyExternalDriverFloor` → `readCapped`), so the rule the docblock states for `validation` and `queryTimeoutMs` (absent because nothing reads them) is satisfied in the direction that admits a key: `rowCap` is now read. The docblock on the new member names the authored key it mirrors, the ceiling constant, the default and the inert case (a datasource the engine does not floor), which is what a host author needs to know when registering through the contract rather than the schema. **Holds.**
- **Against the type pin.** `data-engine.test.ts` pins, by mutual `extends`, that `registerDatasourceDef`'s parameter and `listDatasourceDefs`'s element are the one `EngineDatasourceDef` and that an undeclared `external` key stays refused (`@ts-expect-error` on `credentials`). Adding `rowCap?: number` to the contract while objectql's `DatasourceDef` gains the identical member keeps `Registered`/`Listed`/`Declared` resolvable; the `credentials` refusal still holds since `rowCap` is the only key admitted. `Type Check · source gates` on the head is green. **Holds.**
- **Against the scenario, tried to break it:**
  - *Register before the driver, driver before the def, reconnect.* `applyExternalDriverFloor` is called from both doors; the floor is created once and the cap is read from the map on each read, so order does not matter and a reconnect's re-registration (`:1101`, with `opts.previous.external`) restores the previous cap, not a captured one. **Holds.**
  - *Edit the cap on a live datasource.* The admin update path merges `patch.external` whole (`datasource-admin-service.ts:909`) and the stored record is re-parsed against `DatasourceSchema` before persisting, so a new `rowCap` reaches the engine on the next connect; a def re-registered without a reconnect takes effect on the next read. **Holds.**
  - *A host bypasses the schema with `rowCap: 50_000` or `rowCap: '5000'`.* Held at 10,000 and read as 1,000 respectively; the ruling's bound survives every door. **Holds**, with should-fix 2 on silence.
  - *The refusal at the ceiling.* With `cap === EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP_CEILING` the message omits the "raise `external.rowCap`" clause, so a datasource already at the maximum is not told to raise it. Pinned by test. **Holds.**
  - *The count path.* `count` reads through the same `readCapped`, so a raised cap lets the total be computed over the same set the page is drawn from; the guide's "twice per page" cost claim is exactly this. **Holds.**
  - *The conformance kit and the runtime spike test* keep pinning `EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP + 1` for a datasource with no key; `EXTERNAL_ROW_CAP` is still 1,000 by binding, so neither moves. **Holds.**
- **Clamp versus refuse in `resolveExternalRowCap`.** I judged whether holding an out-of-range engine-side value at the ceiling, or falling back to the default on a malformed one, is the lenient consumer shape rule 12 forbids. It is not: the authoring door (the spec) refuses loudly and this reading never widens what an author may write; it guards a public contract member a host can set without the parse, and it errs toward the platform maximum, never past it. What it lacks is a trace: a host that registered `rowCap: 50_000` reads at 10,000 and nothing says so. **Should-fix 2.**

**Must-fix:** none.

**Should-fix:**
1. The `Metadata-protocol:` kind on this PR and its changeset. The authorable key was `added` in #29854; this diff adds no authorable key, value or type and moves no authorable shard, so its kind is `none` (level `patch` on both packages) or, at most, `semantic`. Restate the line in the PR body and the changeset and grade accordingly, or record in the changeset why the seat keeps `added`/`minor` for PR 2 of the split. Gate-green either way; declaration accuracy only.
2. `resolveExternalRowCap` is silent when it holds a value at the ceiling or discards a malformed one. A one-line `logger.warn` through the floor host (which already carries `logger`), once per datasource, would tell an operator whose def bypassed the schema why the datasource reads at a cap they did not write.
3. Follow-up outside this card: a conformance-kit case with a generated fixture above 1,001 rows and a raised-cap floor host, so a driver that hard-codes 1001 is caught by the kit rather than by the guide's sentence. The kit's floors (`writeCase`, `flooredRead`) would pass `rowCap` on the host for that case.

**Check-runs on the head, as read at 2026-11-03 (two reads, a few minutes apart):** at the second read 20 completed success (`Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Auto Label`, `filter`, `Build UI Deps`, `Build Docs`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`); 8 completed skipped (opt-in, schedule and UI-only gates); 33 still in progress (`Test Core` 1-8/8, `Test UI` 1-16/16, `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`). None failed. The verdict below is the contract verdict on the tree; the in-progress families' conclusions are their own gate verdicts and landing waits on them as usual.
